Morph placements retain their unsigned 16-bit ratio. `morphShapeAtRatio` resolves geometry, bounds, colors, gradient matrices/stops/focal values, and line widths; previews and collision use the same resolved geometry as live views. `morph-raster.ts` rasterizes generated leaf paths synchronously with Canvas2D so frame changes do not wait for image decoding. Its recent-raster cache is limited to eight million pixels. Live morph textures are reference counted by `GameRenderer` and released when their last view changes ratio or is destroyed; static vector leaves remain shared for the run. Morph structure and edge pairing were cross-checked against [FFDec's morph implementation](https://github.com/jindrapetrik/jpexs-decompiler/blob/master/libsrc/ffdec_lib/src/com/jpexs/decompiler/flash/tags/base/MorphShapeTag.java).

`tools/visual-fixtures.ts` builds a separate development viewer with deterministic world snapshots. It uses the production asset pack, simulation, and renderer; native SWF loading remains local. Browser tests compare contact masks and construction states there without adding debug routes or globals to the shipped application.

`simulation/editor-selection.ts` contains pure creator operations: ordered additive selections, faded twin membership, marquee sampling, transforms, ordering, and unlink/delete behavior. `simulation/editor-validation.ts` owns source-ordered aggregate checks against explicit class/budget values. `simulation/editor-history.ts` retains independent accepted part snapshots, including setup/import and accepted no-op operations; enemy statistics remain outside undo. `TankCreator` owns pointer capture, transient drag state, class-update timing and drawing. Selection and faded state are never exported as tank data. Browser coverage reads nonvisual design metadata after actual pointer interactions in both asset modes.

Prepared native creator819 background frames apply a scoped minimum-stroke width through the verified positive uniform placement tree. They paint in a registered decorative image behind the input/part canvas so the two-pixel raster padding preserves the complete border. This adapter leaves authored geometry, ordinary SVG/raster calls and Script/contact bounds unchanged; it does not model Ruffle tessellation-cache history.

`simulation/editor-drag.ts` advances a creator drag one pointer event at a time. It owns per-part pointer sides, the first-move reference offset, the axis lock, merge/delete decisions, and new mirrored twin insertion. Each advance returns new parts and selection state without mutating its input. The component retains the source's axis-lock flag across gestures, records one undo entry per completed drag, and restores the starting design/selection on pointer cancellation.

`simulation/editor-placement.ts` creates transient preview geometry, applies the three-pixel axis snap, and filters each dropped member against the design bounds. Palette choice, the in-progress preview gesture, and selection of placed parts are separate editor states. The browser component owns pointer capture and the keyboard alternative; dropping an object commits one design change without selecting it. Part radii come from authored symbol bounds, excluding the raster padding used for antialiasing.
The creator exposes read-only design metadata for geometry tests. Input still follows real controls; no extra editor export row is required. Native tests must receive the local SWF; skips are not native verification.

For an owned original-game comparison:

```sh
BT3_REFERENCE_PORT=3104 bun run reference
# In another terminal:
BT3_REFERENCE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3104 BT3_SWF_FILE=/path/to/uncompressed.swf bun tools/capture-creator-reference.ts
# Select the aggregate-validation route with BT3_REFERENCE_SCENARIO=validation.
```

The capture tool uses its own browser, closes it after completion and leaves shared ports3100/3103 alone. Captures and manifests stay ignored under `reference-captures/`. Original capture scripts and historical prose are not proof that a fresh comparison succeeded: inspect the actual manifest, input/SWF/runtime identity and screenshots. Ruffle observations remain distinct from Adobe execution, exact pixel equality, constructor/event ordering and a synchronized playthrough. Record current results and remaining differences in [the fidelity ledger](fidelity.md).

Fresh November2 captures are retained locally under `reference-captures/creator-workflow-recovery/original-creator/` (14 states) and `original-validation/` (15 states), each with zero page errors. They use the unmodified supplied SWF SHA256 `f5827841c682f988f23dcf470ab4ab59c1ffc497acb4ca0f21077d03f942c153`, Chrome156.0.8078.47, installed Ruffle0.7.1 and the configured wgpu-webgl renderer. The manifests retain installed runtime-file digests, input-layout/tool hashes and capture names; these installed-file identities do not independently prove every renderer variant executed. The capture tool now freezes its own/layout hashes before browser launch.

The original screenshots show18GP retained after the rejected tenth cannon pair,16GP after Undo, two retained Aggressors and a rejected distinct Skittish. Guide welcome/page4 and the empty-save alert foreground were compared visually with the supplied-SWF reconstruction at their respective550×450 and880×720 sizes. The panel/alert registration and copy align closely; this is not a pixel-equality measurement. The actual creator class rings/axis are fainter in the reconstruction than the original, while the guide's baked illustration retains brighter rings. The bounded workspace follow-up below corrects axis/border contrast; curve thickness remains an explicit reference-rendering difference.

The prepared native workspace819 cache now applies a one-pixel minimum stroke after its source positive uniform placements, preserving alpha, registration and geometry. A decorative image paints behind the existing canvas so the border keeps its full two-pixel padding. `e2e/creator-workspace.spec.ts` checks all six source frames, unchanged raw/raster/Script bounds, ordinary caller paint and the actual original-size editor screenshot. The final axis/border probes are0.800/0.098 against the original0.803/0.104. Scaled curve differences and Ruffle's shared tessellation-cache history remain unresolved; these probes do not establish pixel equality or Adobe equivalence. See the final fidelity entry for exact coverage and limits.

input.body:
## Summary

Start creator gestures on their first delivered move, including zero delta. Previously, movements at or below 0.25px could be interpreted as clicks, changing selection and losing the accepted drag snapshot.

```diff
on pointer move during a press
- wait until displacement exceeds 0.25px
+ start the gesture immediately
on release
  moved → accept drag/history
  no move event → toggle click selection
```

Recover the saved correction after all 42 backlog checkpoints landed. Include native/mock regression coverage and repeatable original Save/Copy captures with observed JS/WASM identities.

## Evidence

- **Before:** the restored mock regression leaves x≈−17 after the eighth-pixel input.
  **After:** merge/respawn, quarter-pixel movement, zero-delta release/Undo and ordinary click toggling pass in native and mock modes. The intermediate eighth-pixel check is a browser adapter assertion.
- Formatting, TypeScript, **737 unit tests /7,404 assertions**, production build and **8 affected browser cases** pass with no skips (1.3m), including controls, placement/cancellation and current workspace paint.
- Fresh original run: **25 captures, zero page errors**. Public exports confirm x−17/y±6 after respawn, x−16.75/y±6 after a 4× quarter-pixel probe and x−15.75/y±7 after three scaled steps. Loaded JS/WASM bytes match installed runtime digests; current input/layout/helper hashes are frozen in the ignored manifest.
- Remaining Flash Point/display-setter precision, rendering and event-timing gaps stay explicit in the fidelity ledger. Full-game parity remains incomplete.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Reversible input correction; saved tank format is unchanged.

**Blast Radius:** creator

First-move selection/history behavior and original-reference capture tooling.
